title: Data-Driven Probabilistic Air-Sea Flux Parameterization
processes: ocean surface boundary layer vertical mixing
parameterization_target: turbulent air-sea momentum and heat fluxes (tau_x, tau_y, Q_S, Q_L)
testbed_rationale: Uses a curated benchmark of ~10,000 shipboard eddy-covariance flux observations alongside an implementation in the open-source single-column ocean model GOTM at OWS Papa, with open code and weights on Zenodo.
pain_points: Scarcity of direct in-situ eddy-covariance flux measurements, especially at high wind speeds (>15 m/s) and under large air-sea temperature differences
Geographical sampling imbalance, with more than 50% of cruise observations collected in tropical regions
Inability to directly resolve height dependence because measurements are taken at heights where vertical gradients vanish
Distinguishing observational/sampling measurement uncertainty from missing subgrid physics or unobserved state variables
extraction_notes: The single-column ocean model GOTM experiments are 1D forced sensitivity experiments where the fluxes are prescribed boundary forcings without two-way state variable feedback to the flux algorithm, hence online_coupled is marked false.
